issues.problem: Glossary: ṛta = order (ऋत in Hindi); 'सत्य' deviates.

Reads as a prohibition ('let the waters not rest'); English says 'did not come to rest', and ramanta is a past injunctive/impf. Also the Hindi fuses savitre into Indra ('प्रेरक इन्द्र ... जो अहि का हनन करनेवाला है'), whereas English has three separate datives.
issues.fix: ऋत करनेवाले देव के लिए, प्रेरक के लिए, अहि का हनन करनेवाले इन्द्र के लिए जल नहीं रुके।

patch.old: सत्य को रचनेवाले देव के लिए, प्रेरक इन्द्र के लिए, जो अहि का हनन करनेवाला है, जल रुके नहीं।
patch.new: ऋत करनेवाले देव के लिए, प्रेरक के लिए, अहि का हनन करनेवाले इन्द्र के लिए जल नहीं रुके।

issues.problem: savitre next to devāya kṛṇvate and Indra is most naturally the god Savitṛ; the glossary writes divine names in plain IAST (Savitṛ). The draft's own note says so. Decide; if Savitṛ, change English, gloss, Hindi (सविता). No patch.
'धाराएँ' (streams) is an interpretation; dhunayaḥ is 'roaring ones'.

issues.problem: Printed viduṣa u- allows viduṣe (dat., 'to the knowing one') + uvāca by the same e-before-vowel sandhi the draft itself uses for upāyane (2.28.2); that gives 'the mother declared him to the knowing one' and removes the unnamed 'knowing one' of the notes. Mention as alternative in notes; no patch.
Hindi 'like a burning stone' differs from English 'with burning, as it were with a stone' (tapuṣā aśnā iva).
'इच्छा' (desire) is added; pṛṇāt is 'satisfies/fills'; English says 'satisfies me'.
'nothing' is an unmarked subject; the verbs are bare 3 sg. subjunctives.
issues.fix: May it not exhaust me, nor tire me, nor make me slack

Others: gir/sumna glossary deviations in unit 11, unmarked subject in unit 7, Hindi/English mismatch in unit 4, alternative viduṣe in unit 2. Units 3, 5, 6, 8, 9 ok. No regrouping suggested.
